evidence.claim: The IMF said Indonesia’s authorities had responded with a bold, comprehensive, well-coordinated policy package that maintained economic and financial stability, and it welcomed gradual withdrawal of extraordinary support, a return to the fiscal rule, and using subsidy savings to strengthen the social safety net.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Indonesia
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said Indonesia’s authorities had responded with a bold, comprehensive, well-coordinated policy package that maintained economic and financial stability, and it welcomed gradual withdrawal of extraordinary support, a return to the fiscal rule, and using subsidy savings to strengthen the social safety net.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official IMF surveillance summary with explicit policy assessment and recommendations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers Indonesia’s 2022 macro-policy environment and the inherited recovery phase.
evidence.ruler_attribution: High for fiscal and macro-policy choices under Jokowi, but not exclusive credit because BI, accumulated buffers, and global conditions mattered.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also says the outlook remained tilted to the downside and recovery benefited from accumulated policy buffers.
Some positive outcomes were not uniquely Jokowi’s; they also reflected pre-existing buffers and external conditions.

evidence.claim: BPS reported that Indonesia’s 2022 economy grew 5.31 percent, with GDP per capita of Rp71.0 million or US$4,783.9, and that transportation/storage and exports were the leading growth components.
evidence.title: Ekonomi Indonesia Tahun 2022 Tumbuh 5,31 Persen
evidence.excerpt: BPS reported that Indonesia’s 2022 economy grew 5.31 percent, with GDP per capita of Rp71.0 million or US$4,783.9, and that transportation/storage and exports were the leading growth components.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official national statistics release with clear 2022 macro indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Low-to-moderate because this is an aggregate national outcome affected by reopening, commodities, and external demand as well as policy.
contrary_evidence: The statistic itself does not isolate Jokowi’s contribution.
The growth mix was heavily influenced by sectors and external conditions beyond the presidency.

evidence.claim: BPS reported that the August 2022 open unemployment rate was 5.86 percent, down 0.63 points from August 2021, while average labor wages were Rp3.07 million per month and employment increased by 4.25 million people year on year.
evidence.title: Agustus 2022: Tingkat Pengangguran Terbuka (TPT) sebesar 5,86 persen dan Rata-rata upah buruh sebesar 3,07 juta rupiah per bulan
evidence.excerpt: BPS reported that the August 2022 open unemployment rate was 5.86 percent, down 0.63 points from August 2021, while average labor wages were Rp3.07 million per month and employment increased by 4.25 million people year on year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official labor-force survey release with direct 2022 labor-market figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Low-to-moderate because this is an economy-wide outcome shaped by recovery, not a ruler-only decision.
contrary_evidence: The release is a snapshot, not a causal policy audit.
It still shows underemployment and pandemic scarring, so household security was improving but not solved.

evidence.claim: BPS reported that the poverty rate in September 2022 was 9.57 percent, or 26.36 million people, slightly higher than March 2022 but lower than September 2021.
evidence.title: Persentase Penduduk Miskin September 2022 naik menjadi 9,57 persen
evidence.excerpt: BPS reported that the poverty rate in September 2022 was 9.57 percent, or 26.36 million people, slightly higher than March 2022 but lower than September 2021.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistics release with direct poverty data and comparison points.
evidence.period_fit: Directly reports a target-year household welfare outcome as of September 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Low-to-moderate because poverty is an aggregate outcome influenced by many factors, though policy responses to inflation and transfers matter.
contrary_evidence: Poverty rose slightly from March 2022, so the household picture was not uniformly improving.
The measure reflects broad conditions, not Jokowi’s actions alone.

evidence.claim: BPS reported that Indonesia’s September 2022 Gini ratio was 0.381, down from 0.384 in March 2022 and unchanged from September 2021.
evidence.title: Gini Ratio September 2022 tercatat sebesar 0,381
evidence.excerpt: BPS reported that Indonesia’s September 2022 Gini ratio was 0.381, down from 0.384 in March 2022 and unchanged from September 2021.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official inequality statistics release with explicit comparison points.
evidence.period_fit: Directly reports a target-year distributional outcome.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Low-to-moderate because inequality is shaped by many structural factors, though transfer policy and inflation response can affect it.
contrary_evidence: The change was small, so the distributional improvement was modest.
The measure does not isolate any single policy, leader, or region.

evidence.claim: Jokowi issued Inpres 4/2022 to accelerate elimination of extreme poverty by 2024 through integrated, targeted coordination across ministries and local governments, including education aid, health access, stunting reduction, sanitation, PBI JKN enrollment, clean water, housing, and data targeting.
evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Keluarkan Inpres 4/2022 tentang Percepatan Penghapusan Kemiskinan Ekstrem
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi issued Inpres 4/2022 to accelerate elimination of extreme poverty by 2024 through integrated, targeted coordination across ministries and local governments, including education aid, health access, stunting reduction, sanitation, PBI JKN enrollment, clean water, housing, and data targeting.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential instruction text reproduced by the cabinet secretariat with detailed ministry tasks and dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi personally as the issuing president and direct commander of the relevant ministries.
contrary_evidence: Implementation still depended on ministries and local governments; the instruction itself does not prove delivery quality.

evidence.claim: Jokowi said more than 70 percent of fuel subsidies were benefiting better-off car owners and announced reallocation to targeted support, including BLT BBM for 20.65 million poor families and wage subsidies for 16 million workers.
evidence.title: Pernyataan Pers Presiden RI mengenai Pengalihan Subsidi BBM
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi said more than 70 percent of fuel subsidies were benefiting better-off car owners and announced reallocation to targeted support, including BLT BBM for 20.65 million poor families and wage subsidies for 16 million workers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with specific budget and beneficiary counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi because he announced and justified the reallocation himself.
contrary_evidence: The move was a response to inflationary pressure and fiscal burden, not a clean prosperity windfall.

evidence.claim: Regsosek was a nationwide socioeconomic registration covering housing, clean water sanitation, asset ownership, vulnerability of special groups, geospatial information, and welfare levels, intended to rank welfare and improve government intervention effectiveness.
evidence.title: Initial Registration of Regsosek Begins
evidence.excerpt: Regsosek was a nationwide socioeconomic registration covering housing, clean water sanitation, asset ownership, vulnerability of special groups, geospatial information, and welfare levels, intended to rank welfare and improve government intervention effectiveness.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official BPS news release describing a concrete nationwide data system and its intended use.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national government and BPS under Jokowi’s administration, though operational execution was statistical rather than personal presidential action.
contrary_evidence: The page explains the system design, not the quality of subsequent targeting or outcomes.

evidence.claim: Jokowi said he appointed Zulkifli Hasan and Hadi Tjahjanto based on track record, experience, and managerial skill to solve problems in detail.
evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Ungkap Alasan Penunjukan Zulkifli Hasan dan Hadi Tjahjanto
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi said he appointed Zulkifli Hasan and Hadi Tjahjanto based on track record, experience, and managerial skill to solve problems in detail.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official transcript of Jokowi's own explanation for cabinet appointments, with concrete quoted rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi because the appointment rationale is his own public justification.
contrary_evidence: A competence-based rationale does not exclude coalition balancing or patronage motives.

evidence.claim: The trade minister was removed after soaring cooking-oil prices and shortages, with the crisis linked to arrests of Trade Ministry officials and palm-oil businessmen allegedly involved in graft.
evidence.title: Jokowi orders seventh Cabinet reshuffle
evidence.excerpt: The trade minister was removed after soaring cooking-oil prices and shortages, with the crisis linked to arrests of Trade Ministry officials and palm-oil businessmen allegedly involved in graft.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable national reporting on the reshuffle, with a clear causal narrative tied to a corruption-tinged supply crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Jokowi's decision to reshuffle and replace the minister after the scandal and shortage crisis.
contrary_evidence: The source also suggests the move was reactive damage control rather than evidence of a clean appointment process.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $750 million loan to help Indonesia increase tax revenue, improve tax system equity, and strengthen institutions for more efficient planning and spending; the package is framed as supporting tax policy and administration reforms.
evidence.title: New Support Will Help Strengthen Indonesia’s Tax System, Improve Development Spending
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $750 million loan to help Indonesia increase tax revenue, improve tax system equity, and strengthen institutions for more efficient planning and spending; the package is framed as supporting tax policy and administration reforms.
evidence.source_locator: Press release lead and paragraphs describing the two reform pillars
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with specific financing and reform details; strong temporal fit to 2022 policy execution.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Jokowi’s 2019-2024 administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level fiscal reform under Jokowi’s administration; not a personal act by Jokowi alone, but within executive policy control.
contrary_evidence: World Bank notes Indonesia’s tax revenues were still low versus peers.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to support Indonesia’s human capital agenda by safeguarding income protection, increasing access to healthcare services, preventing unhealthy behavior, and improving the effectiveness of government spending; it also said Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020 but remained below peers.
evidence.title: New Financing Will Support Indonesia to Improve and Protect Human Capital
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $350 million loan to support Indonesia’s human capital agenda by safeguarding income protection, increasing access to healthcare services, preventing unhealthy behavior, and improving the effectiveness of government spending; it also said Indonesia’s Human Capital Index improved from 0.50 to 0.54 between 2010 and 2020 but remained below peers.
evidence.source_locator: Press release lead and human capital paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with clear policy content, funding amount, and time fit.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 policy support and retrospective human-capital comparison relevant to the Jokowi period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level reform agenda; attribution to Jokowi is indirect but real through executive control of social and fiscal policy.
contrary_evidence: World Bank says education, social insurance, and stunting remained weak relative to peers.

evidence.claim: President Jokowi said BLT BBM distribution had reached 19.7 million beneficiaries, or 95.9 percent of the target, after the government reallocated fuel subsidies to maintain purchasing power.
evidence.title: Cash Direct Assistance Distribution for Fuel Oil Subsidy Reallocation Reaches up to 95.9 Percent
evidence.excerpt: President Jokowi said BLT BBM distribution had reached 19.7 million beneficiaries, or 95.9 percent of the target, after the government reallocated fuel subsidies to maintain purchasing power.
evidence.source_locator: Paragraph quoting the President after observing distribution in Baubau
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential statement with a specific implementation metric and date.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 implementation evidence within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Jokowi’s announced policy shift and oversight of rollout, though execution was carried out by ministries and post offices.
contrary_evidence: The measure is short-term relief; it does not prove long-run efficiency or equitable targeting by itself.

evidence.claim: The 2022 State Budget deficit was 2.38 percent of GDP, smaller than the target stated in law, and fiscal consolidation was achieved faster than planned.
evidence.title: Economic Minister: State Budget Deficit Smaller than Target
evidence.excerpt: The 2022 State Budget deficit was 2.38 percent of GDP, smaller than the target stated in law, and fiscal consolidation was achieved faster than planned.
evidence.source_locator: Quoted statement by Coordinating Minister Airlangga Hartarto after the cabinet meeting led by President Jokowi
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government summary of a fiscal year outcome with a precise deficit figure and date.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on fiscal year 2022; directly relevant to Jokowi’s 2022 economic management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Jokowi administration’s fiscal policy and cabinet coordination; not solely to Jokowi personally.
contrary_evidence: Deficit performance partly benefited from stronger revenue conditions and cyclical recovery.

evidence.claim: BPK gave an unqualified opinion on the central government’s 2022 financial statements; 81 of 82 line ministries and the state treasury statements also received unqualified opinions, and BPK said most fiscal-transparency criteria were met, while noting audit findings totaling Rp25.85 trillion.
evidence.title: BPK Gives Unqualified Opinion on 2022 Financial Statements of Central Government
evidence.excerpt: BPK gave an unqualified opinion on the central government’s 2022 financial statements; 81 of 82 line ministries and the state treasury statements also received unqualified opinions, and BPK said most fiscal-transparency criteria were met, while noting audit findings totaling Rp25.85 trillion.
evidence.source_locator: Press release body and transparency paragraph
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary audit-board release on FY2022 accounts with concrete audit outcomes and transparency language.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective FY2022 evidence; directly relevant to Jokowi’s administrative and fiscal management record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-wide financial management under Jokowi’s cabinet; the audit is not personal proof but is strong evidence of implementation quality.
contrary_evidence: BPK also reported material findings and internal-control weaknesses, so the result is positive but not clean.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said extended school closures and disrupted reopenings affected around 60 million students in Indonesia and caused significant learning loss, with harms especially acute for vulnerable students.
evidence.title: As children in Indonesia return to school, UNICEF calls for urgent action to address learning crisis
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said extended school closures and disrupted reopenings affected around 60 million students in Indonesia and caused significant learning loss, with harms especially acute for vulnerable students.
evidence.source_locator: First and second paragraphs of the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF is a strong independent source on education disruptions, and the claim is specific and contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, though the shock is partly inherited from the pandemic rather than uniquely Jokowi’s creation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attribution to Jokowi is limited; this is mainly a constraint and implementation challenge for the administration’s recovery response rather than a ruler-caused collapse.
contrary_evidence: The article primarily reflects pandemic inheritance; it does not isolate Jokowi’s personal policy failure.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said Indonesia had made remarkable poverty-reduction progress and extreme poverty was basically eradicated by 2022, but more than one-third of Indonesians remained economically insecure and could be pushed into poverty by shocks; it urged broader opportunity creation, protection, and resilience investments.
evidence.title: Indonesia Poverty Assessment: Pathway Towards Economic Security
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Indonesia had made remarkable poverty-reduction progress and extreme poverty was basically eradicated by 2022, but more than one-third of Indonesians remained economically insecure and could be pushed into poverty by shocks; it urged broader opportunity creation, protection, and resilience investments.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent World Bank assessment with explicit 2022 retrospective and policy interpretation.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 conditions and policy trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Broadly attributable to the Jokowi period, but the result reflects long-run reform, commodity conditions, and recovery as well as current administration choices.
contrary_evidence: The assessment says economic insecurity remained high, so the progress is real but incomplete.

evidence.claim: Jokowi said the government had started infrastructure work in the core Nusantara capital area, that the raw-water dam would be completed in January, and that ministry, presidential, and vice-presidential buildings would begin construction in December.
evidence.title: Presiden Jokowi Sampaikan Progres Pembangunan IKN
evidence.excerpt: Jokowi said the government had started infrastructure work in the core Nusantara capital area, that the raw-water dam would be completed in January, and that ministry, presidential, and vice-presidential buildings would begin construction in December.
evidence.source_locator: Lead paragraph and presidential quotes in the news item
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential update with direct statements on 2022 implementation milestones.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to a flagship Jokowi program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Jokowi as a personal flagship policy and executive priority, although much implementation was delegated to ministries and the IKN authority.
contrary_evidence: This is initiation evidence, not completion; success depended on later delivery and financing.

evidence.claim: WHO said Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage in 2022, exceeding the national target of 94.1 percent, and that the BIAN catch-up campaign reached 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines, 1.3 million with polio vaccines, and 2 million with DTP-HB-Hib vaccines.
evidence.title: Indonesia Targets Low Vaccination Areas to Tackle Decline in Childhood Immunization
evidence.excerpt: WHO said Indonesia achieved 94.6 percent full immunization coverage in 2022, exceeding the national target of 94.1 percent, and that the BIAN catch-up campaign reached 26.5 million children with measles-rubella vaccines, 1.3 million with polio vaccines, and 2 million with DTP-HB-Hib vaccines.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO retrospective on 2022 national immunization performance with precise coverage and campaign figures.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on 2022 campaign and coverage; acceptable as target-period evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Jokowi’s administration through Ministry of Health coordination, though the campaign was operationally carried by health officials and local governments.
contrary_evidence: WHO also noted outbreaks in low-vaccination areas, so the win was uneven and not fully durable.
